identity.entry_type_evidence: Official California Privacy Protection Agency page for the Delete Request and Opt-out Platform.
identity.single_request_coverage_evidence: The page says DROP lets a person send one request to over 600 registered data brokers. It does not list those brokers on the inspected summary, and it does not say every catalog row is included.
documented_request_eligibility: The person must be a California resident, verified through the California Identity Gateway. Login.gov is optional and only suggested if an account already exists. A parent or family member may submit for some other California residents.

discovery.profile_identification: The person creates a DROP profile. The page says the person chooses how much basic information to provide.

steps.evidence: DROP page section Eligibility and verification.

steps.action: Submit one DROP request to registered data brokers. The form was not submitted.
steps.evidence: DROP page step Submit your DROP request.

request_workflow.documented_processing_time: Starting August 1, 2026, data brokers must access DROP at least once every 45 days. The page says status updates could take up to 90 days and that brokers must delete data every 45 days.
request_workflow.published_request_limits: The inspected summary says the request goes to registered data brokers in DROP, not to every company in this catalog.

automation.classification_evidence: DROP is an official one-to-many deletion and opt-out platform, but eligibility verification uses the California Identity Gateway. The research GET hit a Cloudflare interstitial.
automatable_steps: Explain eligibility and the 45-day and 90-day timing. Do not collect identity-gateway data into a broker adapter.
human_steps: Choose the profile details and submit the request.

verification.evidence_notes: Regulator platform, not a single broker's form. Coverage of this catalog was not matched broker by broker. No request submitted.
